stories.headline: Shannon Larp called all six and got all six
stories.body:
The desk went on the record on Friday, one winner in every matchup, and week two is now finished. Shannon Larp went six for six. Stephen B Smith, Mina Crimes and Skip Baseless all went five and one. Fat McCafferty went one and five.

Four of the five desks had The Shortbus Superstars beating davidbatista. David won 119.30 to 104.14, and that one game is the entire difference between six for six and five and one — Larp was the only man in the building who took davidbatista. It is also the team McCafferty picked to win the championship.

McCafferty's one correct call was littlescot229, who beat Kool-Aid Man 134.18 to 109.98. His other five all lost, and one of them lost because the team he was fading scored 56.00 on Monday night.

takes.text: Six for six, and I want to say plainly what it is worth, which is not very much. I took every favourite in the building. That is not a read on a league, it is a read on a table somebody else built. Ask me again in a week where the favourites lose.

FIVE AND ONE! And I said on Friday that Chase loses this week, out loud, when this desk was still treating that matchup like a coin flip! Carlzyn by twenty-three! I do not want the six, I want the one nobody else would say.

I read the projection straight down with no editorialising and it went five and one. Larp read the favourites and went six and nothing. On six games that is noise, and anybody drawing a conclusion from one week of this is doing the thing I spend my life asking people not to do.

Five and one, and the one is a team that has now lost two games by a combined eighty-three points. I will wear that. What I will not wear is the idea that Larp winning this week means anything, because Larp will take six favourites again next week and one of them is going to fall over.

One and five. I have seen the number. I am aware of the number. Four of those five were teams that were behind when I took them, which is the entire point of taking them, and one week does not settle a thing I said about November. Write it down.

stories.storyline: Does Larp keep taking favourites, and does anybody beat six for six?

stories.headline: Blake needed 28.46 from three men and got 56.00 with his quarterback hurt
stories.body:
Chop Wood, Carry Water went into Monday night on 70.10 against a finished 98.56, needing 28.46 from Jaxson Dart, Kyren Williams and Davante Adams. They produced 56.00 and won 126.10 to 98.56.

Adams did most of it: 39.50 against a 13.7 projection. Kyren Williams added 15.70. Dart, who was carrying a knee designation and is listed as out, managed 0.80 of a projected 21.1 — so Blake covered a twenty-eight point deficit with two players while the third produced almost nothing.

Skip Baseless said on Monday morning that he was not moving. He had Chop Wood, Carry Water in his called shots and he has them as his championship pick, and both survived the night. Patrick Mahomes scored 34.98 on the bench for the second week running, which is the part of this that has not changed.

takes.text: I said I would not blink and I did not blink. Thirty-nine and a half from Davante Adams, on a Monday, with my quarterback on one leg. Everybody in this building spent the weekend waiting for me to fold and I want each of them to say my name out loud this week.

He is RIGHT and he is right for the WRONG REASON! He benched Mahomes for thirty-five! Again! Two weeks, seventy points of quarterback on his own bench, and the man wins anyway and now I have to listen to him! This is the worst outcome available to me personally.

Fifty points of projection against a 28.46 deficit was live and I said so. What I did not price, because nobody can, is 39.50 from a receiver projected for 13.7. He needed one outlier and he got one. That is a good result, not a good process, and the bench is still where the process is.

stories.storyline: Does Blake start Mahomes in week three, or is 85% efficiency just how this team runs?

stories.headline: Puka Nacua never took the field
stories.body:
Fat McCafferty spent Monday saying his whole position came down to one receiver. It did, and the receiver did not play. Puka Nacua was listed out with a hip and finished on 0.00.

The Shortbus Superstars lost 104.14 to 119.30 and are 0-2, twelfth in the power rankings with a 3% playoff estimate. They got 21.70 from Stefon Diggs and 17.20 from Sam LaPorta and still had the second-lowest score of the week. Jordan Love scored 17.80 on the bench.

That is the team McCafferty has picked to win the championship, and he does not get to change it.

takes.text: He did not play. That is not a man being wrong about a football team, that is a hip. I said the pick was about November and the calendar has not reached October. Nothing that happened on Monday night told me anything, because on Monday night nothing happened.

This is the part nobody accounts for when they make a pick in September. You can be right about a roster for three months and lose the argument to a hip in week two. It does not make the pick smart and it does not make it stupid. It just means we learned nothing.

Zero and two, twelfth in the rankings, three percent to make the playoffs, and the man is on this desk telling us to wait until November. I have a championship pick I am defending too, and mine scored a hundred and twenty-six last night.

stories.storyline: How long does 0-2 and twelfth stay a November argument?

stories.headline: Nine starters left their games hurt and five of the six winners had one
stories.body:
Fifteen starters across this league carried an injury designation in week two and nine of them finished so far under their projection that they almost certainly left the game or played through something.

Caleb Williams, out with a hamstring, returned 8.72 of a projected 22.0 and F&F: Tokyo Swift won anyway, 133.32 to 122.68. DJ Moore, out with a shoulder, returned minus 0.10 and Team Carlzyn won by 23.46. Alec Pierce, out with a heel, returned 2.10 and littlescot229 won by 24.20. Jayden Reed, out with a neck, returned 1.40 and davidbatista won by 15.16. Jaxson Dart's 0.80 is above. Five of the six winning teams had a starter leave hurt.

It cut the other way too. Malik Nabers, carrying a shoulder, returned 1.10 of a projected 13.6 for the team named after him, and Chase lost by 23.46. Saquon Barkley returned 3.00 of 16.6 for Dsteady1234. Neither result was close enough for one player to have changed it.

takes.text: Nine of fifteen designated starters produced under forty percent of their projection. That is not a scoring story, it is an availability story, and availability is the one variable none of us price and all of us get judged on. Two weeks in and it has already cost more points in this league than any lineup decision has.

I have been the man carried off and I have been the man who had to keep playing next to the empty locker. Nobody in this league lost a game because somebody was soft. Chase drafted a receiver, started him, and watched a shoulder take the week off him. There is no lesson in it.

FIVE of the SIX winners had a man walk off hurt and they won ANYWAY! Which tells me the six teams that lost did not lose to bad luck, they lost because they were behind before anybody got hurt! Do not hand me an injury report as an alibi!

stories.storyline: Does anybody in this league adjust for availability, or does everybody keep drafting for a full season?

stories.headline: Darrien left 73.8 on the bench, including 35.98 from a quarterback
stories.body:
Dsteady1234 finished on 98.56, the lowest score of the week, and left 73.8 points unstarted. Matthew Stafford scored 35.98 on the bench. Tre Tucker added 22.90.

The lineup Darrien did start returned 77% of what was available to him, the worst figure in the league. He is 0-2 with an all-play record of 3-19, and he lost a game he was leading at kickoff on Monday night.

For contrast, The Dak Pack posted 159.16 — the highest score in the league — while leaving 63.3 unstarted, Dalton Kincaid's 22.50 among it. There is more than one way to not start your best team.

takes.text: THIRTY-FIVE POINT NINE EIGHT FROM A QUARTERBACK HE DID NOT START! Seventy-three points on the bench! He lost by twenty-seven! I could pick nine names out of that roster with my eyes closed and beat the nine he chose!

Seventy-three on the bench and he still scored ninety-eight. There is a roster there. Nobody in this building will say it because the record is nothing and two, but the points exist and the points are the asset. Write it down.

stories.storyline: Is Darrien's 77% a lineup problem he can fix, or the start of a lost season?
